reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it explains paid pool or share purchases, cycle rewards, and improved returns as participation grows, including a $200 cycle example. It ties benefits and percentage commissions to recruiting users whose purchases and downstream team activity generate rewards. The closing slide directs viewers to BitClub's site to connect.

opening.argument: Judge, the narration does not present every projected return as certain. It qualifies its market discussion with “if the market keeps going” and describes rewards as depending on rating. Even its cycle example starts with a hypothetical structure, not an account statement showing money received. That uncertainty matters: explaining how a proposed bonus is calculated is not the same as guaranteeing that a viewer will earn it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited invitation commission establishes what the presentation says its rules are; it does not establish that a viewer will receive the illustrated return. The cycle slide likewise diagrams a calculation, while the spoken discussion makes rewards dependent on rating. The closing site reference offers a place to learn more, but does not itself make the hypothetical payout certain.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional language does not undo the solicitation. The narration says the binary structure will automatically produce a bonus and a daily reward, then urges attention to building that structure. The case rests on paid purchases and recruitment-linked payouts, not on a claim that every payout is guaranteed.

opening.argument: Judge, the video identifies itself as a detailed analysis and proceeds through worked mechanics: ratings, credits on two branches, and what remains after two cycles. Its team slides lay out percentages by position, and the speaker even calls the generation calculation complicated. Those are features of a demonstration explaining an operating model. A tutorial can describe commissions, including unattractive ones, without its explanation alone proving that viewers are being induced to join.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies purchase and invitation rules, but those are also the rules an operational walkthrough would have to explain. Its cited first-purchase percentage describes one component, not an instruction to the viewer to buy a share. Even the closing invitation to visit a site is described in the narration as a route to instructions about how the company works.

there, respectively, is video instruction that this is for the company and how it works and so on

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough does more than neutrally map a system. It tells viewers to focus on building their structure, describes accumulating daily rewards from it, and supplies a site where they can connect to the company. The worked examples serve a recruitment-linked earning pitch rather than changing its character.

opening.argument: Judge, the described transactions are purchases of named mining pools, with stated prices and referral percentages. The presentation ties credits to particular pool purchases and distinguishes a first-purchase commission from later team bonuses. That is compatible with a commercial referral program; the supplied material does not show a viewer handing over credentials or demonstrate that any purchased pool is fictitious. Its commission structure merits scrutiny, but the existence of referrals alone does not settle whether the underlying purchase is a sham.

as soon as a person purchased a pole for $ 500 you get 3 credit
Bitclub Network - a real mining company, operating in the market since 2014 and continuing to gain popularity.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening shows that rewards are linked to purchases and recruited teams; it does not show that the pools themselves fail to exist. The description claims a mining business, and the narration names specific pool purchases. The closing destination could therefore be read as a commercial information and signup site, although its presence does not independently verify the business.

citations.quote: Bitclub Network - a real mining company, operating in the market since 2014 and continuing to gain popularity.
purchase a pool for 500, 1000, or 2000
there is a website you can connect to in this company, bitclub.plus

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description's assertion of a real company does not verify its pools. More importantly, this is not merely a single-level referral discount: the presentation makes team rank depend on recruiting participants, awards percentages on their purchases, and extends rewards to purchases deeper in the structure. Those are the mechanisms the video promotes, whether or not a viewer is asked for credentials.
